name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz under attack; Red Sea disrupted
summary: Hormuz transits recover to 26+ a day to 19 Nov as Iranian attacks on tankers intensify; Red Sea fighting continues
state: Vortexa data reported by Bloomberg on 26 Nov show tankers crossing Hormuz above 26 a day on a seven-day average through 19 Nov, up from below 25 on most October days, while Iran intensified attacks and added tugboats to its no-transit list; insurance costs are near wartime highs (gCaptain). The Saudi-led coalition said on 27 Nov it downed a Houthi drone aimed at Riyadh (Al Jazeera). Two chokepoints remain disrupted.
for_you: Shipping disruption in the Gulf and Red Sea can delay deliveries and raise costs for imported goods and fuel. Mariners should follow UKMTO guidance.
rubric_hit: Hormuz materially impeded by attacks, with Red Sea disrupted: two chokepoints

sources.title: Bloomberg — Hormuz tanker traffic rises this month even as attacks increase

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
